LESSON: READING 9.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: GRADE APPROPRIATE FICTION MATERIALS - CHARACTER

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.2: Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Grade appropriate fiction Materials - Character

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Grade appropriate fiction Materials - Character. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: why. 1. What makes reading enjoyable?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the characters in a given fiction text
2. describe the traits of a given character in a fictional text
3. appreciate the role of characters in fiction

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 9.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: GRADE APPROPRIATE FICTION MATERIALS - CHARACTER
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Grade appropriate fiction Materials - Character helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 9.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: GRADE APPROPRIATE FICTION MATERIALS - CHARACTER
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify the characters in a given fiction text

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the characters in a given fiction text. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the characters in a given fiction text.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Grade appropriate fiction Materials - Character”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the characters in a given fiction text. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Describe the traits of a given character in a fictional text

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the traits of a given character in a fictional text. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the traits of a given character in a fictional text.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Grade appropriate fiction Materials - Character to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the traits of a given character in a fictional text. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the role of characters in fiction

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the role of characters in fiction. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the role of characters in fiction.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the role of characters in fiction. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Grade appropriate fiction Materials - Character is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Grade appropriate fiction Materials - Character”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify the characters in a given fiction text)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Grade appropriate fiction Materials - Character to a partner. (skill: describe the traits of a given character in a fictional text)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the role of characters in fiction)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Grade appropriate fiction Materials - Character to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify the characters in a given fiction text.
3. Practise this skill: describe the traits of a given character in a fictional text.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the role of characters in fiction.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Grade appropriate fiction Materials - Character from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Grade appropriate fiction Materials - Character: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Grade appropriate fiction Materials - Character?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. why. 1. What makes reading enjoyable?
2. How can the characters in a story be described?
3. Which stories are the most enjoyable to read?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Grade appropriate fiction Materials - Character means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify the characters in a given fiction text.
5. Be able to: describe the traits of a given character in a fictional text.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
